why: the motif that returns at the close: one server alone in a calm frame, a power line feeding it; a warm haze builds behind it on 'heat' until it fills the space around the box
pull back from the single server: it becomes one of many in racks filling a room, each with its own warm haze; the question sits over the room on 'heat go'
a faint dotted route appears from a chip on the left to the outside of a building on the right, the promise of the path the lesson will light up
the server from b01 in side view: a cool stream enters the front on 'front', crosses the hot parts and turns warm in colour as it goes, leaving the back on 'back'
the warm stream rises from the back of the rack and travels across to a cooling unit; inside the unit it changes colour from warm to cool and flows back toward the rack's front, closing a loop
from the cooling unit a water line carries a warm pulse through the building wall to a generic outdoor unit, which releases it to open air

the whole route so far, server to cooling unit to outside, lights up as one continuous path; a struck-out snowflake tag beside the room on 'not a cold room'; the rack's front and back labels glow again on the rule
the floor plan that holds for the section: a top-down room with four rows of racks, all fronts pointing the same direction, small arrows marking each front
the floor plan holds still with the rows numbered front to back; nothing moves during the silence

the plan runs: the warm stream from row one flows straight into the fronts of row two, and so on; each row's stream is a shade warmer than the last, the back row the warmest; then the whole room tints too cold on 'over-cooled'
the same floor plan: alternate rows rotate in place; the aisle between two fronts tints cool and is labelled on 'cold aisle', the aisle between two backs tints warm and is labelled on 'hot aisle'

the same plan runs again: cool streams enter the cold aisles and pass through the racks, warm streams gather in the hot aisles and travel back to cooling units at the room's edge; no stream crosses another
zoom from the plan to one rack face-on; one gap between servers is picked out in the accent on 'left empty'
the rack in side section: a warm stream from the hot side curls through the empty slot and joins the cool stream entering the servers' fronts, tinting it warm; the term arrives on 'recirculation'
the same side section: a panel slides into the empty slot on 'blanking panel'; the curling warm stream stops and the intake stream returns to cool
back to the floor plan: a thin warm stream spills over the row ends into a cold aisle; then end doors and a roof enclose that aisle on 'containment' and the spill stops
the rack from b13 again, its empty slot open, seen from the aisle as if on a walk-through; a small tag points toward the floor team
the single rack from sec1 returns; its servers are swapped for AI servers one by one and the warm stream at its back swells, much wider than before, overflowing the hot aisle
two equal boxes side by side, one of air and one of water; heat blocks fill them and the air box is full long before the water box
zoom from the rack into one server, then onto one accelerator chip on its board; a cold plate settles onto the chip on 'cold plate' and is shown in cut-away with its channels
cool coolant enters the plate's channels, leaves warm, and travels along a hose out of the server toward the rack's side
follow the warm hose to a cabinet-like unit beside the racks; the unit is labelled CDU on 'the CDU' and its front opens

inside the CDU: the rack loop on the left and the facility water loop on the right, drawn in two distinct colours; heat pulses cross the heat exchanger between them while each liquid stays in its own loop
back out to the server: the cold plate stays lit while a smaller air stream still crosses the other parts; the blanking-panel image from b15 returns beside it
a fraction builds from energy blocks: a tall stack labelled total facility energy on top of the line, a smaller stack labelled IT energy below it
the top stack splits: IT blocks at its base, overhead blocks above them; the cooling block is the largest of the overhead and is labelled on its word
the overhead blocks shrink away until the top stack equals the bottom; the ratio reads 1.0 on its word, then the overhead returns a little and the ratio settles above the floor line
the fraction holds; one short note is pinned beside it on its words, with a small strike mark
small images of the row-to-row exhaust and the empty slot drift into the overhead stack, which grows a little
callback to b01: the same single server, now with the whole liquid path drawn out of it; each hand-off lights in turn just after its word, from the chip to the outdoor unit
the air path lights alongside the liquid path in the same frame, each stage on its word, ending at the same outdoor unit
the full path holds, calm and complete, the room settled; the two short lines rest beside it

b26 puePour shares (it 0.62, cooling 0.26, power losses 0.08, lighting 0.04) are illustrative only: the knowledge sheet carries no split (F21 says cooling is usually the largest overhead, no share). The scene must print no counts, shares or ratio. A human should confirm that the implied split is acceptable.

Temperature code: cool=accent4 teal, warm=accent2 amber in 2D, to match the 3D models' cool/warm roles (kit3d.js). In airflow frames this can put three saturated families on screen (teal, amber, blue) and teal also means 'pos' in this pack. Blue is withheld from airflow frames where possible. The tone check may warn.
